backups.title: Database backups

state.fresh: Newest backup is {{hours}} hours old (limit {{limit}} hours).
state.stale: Newest backup is {{hours}} hours old — older than the {{limit}} hour limit. The backup job is not producing dumps.
state.empty: No backups found in the bucket yet.
state.error: Could not read the backup bucket.
state.misconfigured: Backups are turned on but set up incorrectly, so none are being taken.
state.setupMissing: Backups are turned on but the off-site bucket is not configured yet.
state.unknown: No freshness check has run yet. The worker records one every 6 hours.

reason.futureTimestamp: The newest backup is dated in the future, so its age cannot be trusted. The clock on the machine that made it is probably wrong.

backups.docsHint: If backups are missing or out of date, ask whoever deploys this app to set them up — you cannot enable them from here.

seedPage.title: Load demo data
seedPage.description: Add demo data to your account to explore the app. Available only on development servers.
seedPage.inlineNote: The request stays open until it finishes. Only one load runs at a time.
seedPage.demoDataNote: Adds packages, proposals, an MCP token and finished conversations to your account. Existing records are preserved; running it again does not duplicate them.
seedPage.confirmDescription: This adds demo data to your account on this development server.
seedPage.typePrompt: Type the phrase below to confirm

overview.title: Admin overview
overview.description: Manage users, storage, background jobs and settings.

hint.users: Invite people, change roles, archive or remove accounts.
hint.storage: Disk used by clones and checkouts, against the cap.
hint.jobs: Background jobs, with retry for failed ones.
hint.settings: Sign-up, two-factor policy and the server configuration.

setupBanner.title: This server has no administrator
setupBanner.message: Set <0>ADMIN_EMAILS</0> to your email address and restart the server, then sign up with that address.
setupBanner.errorMessage: The app could not check whether administrators are configured. Review the server logs before publishing.

settings.title: Admin settings
settings.force2faInternalDescription: Required by default. Admin users must set up two-factor authentication before they can use internal tools; a newly created admin account has 24 hours to enroll before it loses access.
settings.force2faPublicDescription: When enabled, signed-in non-admin users must set up two-factor authentication before they can use the application.
settings.force2faAdminWarning: You must enable 2FA for your own account before you can require it for others. Go to Security settings to set it up.
settings.force2faInternalEnabled: Two-factor authentication is now required for administrators
settings.force2faInternalDisabled: Two-factor authentication is no longer required for administrators
settings.force2faPublicEnabled: Two-factor authentication is now required for public users
settings.force2faPublicDisabled: Two-factor authentication is no longer required for public users
settings.updateFailed: Couldn't update that setting. Try again.
settings.signupDescription: Control who can create an account. Invites from the Users page work either way.
settings.signupOpenDescription: When open, anyone who can reach this server can create an account. When closed, only invited people get in.
settings.signupEnvDisabled: SIGNUP_ENABLED is off in the server environment, so sign-up stays closed. Set it to true and restart the server to open sign-up from here.
settings.signupEnvEnabled: SIGNUP_ENABLED is on in the server environment, so this switch decides whether sign-up is open. Turning SIGNUP_ENABLED off closes it whatever this switch says.

runtime.servicesDescription: Set in the server environment. Secrets are never shown here, only whether they are set.
runtime.modelMissing: Questions fail until OPENROUTER_API_KEY and COCKPIT_CONTEXT_MODEL are both set.
runtime.emailMissing: Without email, accounts are not verified and password reset is unavailable.
runtime.backupsMissing: S3 backups are optional and not configured. Without any backup, the Postgres volume is the only copy of accounts, SSH keys, tokens and conversations. Recommended: S3 backups, or at least a manual pg_dump copied off the VPS.
runtime.backupsConfiguredNote: This checks the configuration only. The backup card on the admin overview shows whether dumps actually arrive.
runtime.privacyDescription: How long conversations are kept and who the public privacy notice names as the operator.
runtime.operatorMissing: Set both so the privacy notice names the operator and gives an address for privacy requests. Until then it says they have not been published.
runtime.limitsDescription: The effective values, including defaults. Change them in the server environment and restart.
runtime.rateLimitsDescription: How often each action can be used. A limit cannot be turned off: change its count in the server environment and restart.

rateKeyedOn.user-or-ip: per person, or per IP address when signed out

rateLimits.sshKeyWrite: SSH key generation, import or one-time use
rateLimits.packageWrite: Package source writes and snapshot updates

lsp.title: Code intelligence (LSP)
lsp.description: Language servers give the agent go-to-definition, references and hover. Each one runs in a Landlock sandbox: it can read only the checkout being read and its own files, and write only a private temporary folder.
lsp.filesystemOn: On: only the checkout and the server's own files
lsp.unavailableMissing: The sandbox helper is missing, so code intelligence tools are disabled. Investigations still work with file search and reading. Ask the operator to check the server image; see the language-server sandbox section in the deployment guide.
lsp.unavailableUnsupported: This server's kernel does not offer Landlock (Linux 5.13 or later with landlock in the LSM list), so the LSP tools are disabled. Investigations still work with glob, grep and read. The kernel's reason is below.
lsp.unavailableFailed: The Landlock helper is installed but could not sandbox a test server on this host, so the LSP tools are disabled. Investigations still work with glob, grep and read. The helper reported the message below.
lsp.offWarning: COCKPIT_CONTEXT_LSP_SANDBOX=off: language servers run without the sandbox, so a hostile repository's configuration can make them read files outside its checkout. Use this on development hosts only.
lsp.disabledByCap: COCKPIT_CONTEXT_LSP_MAX_SERVERS is 0, so the LSP tools are off whatever the sandbox reports.

limits.modelStall: Give up on a silent model request after
limits.maxConcurrentRunsPerUser: Concurrent runs per person (overview summaries not counted)
limits.mcpWait: Longest MCP wait for an answer
limits.lspIdle: Stop an idle language server after
limits.maxMcpResultWaitsPerUser: MCP answer waits at once, per person
limits.maxLiveStreamsPerUser: Live run views at once, per person

twoFactorNudge.title: Two-factor authentication is not set up
twoFactorNudge.message: Your admin account signs in with a password alone. Add an authenticator app as a second factor so a stolen password can't unlock this dashboard.
twoFactorNudge.requiredTitle: Two-factor authentication is required for your admin account
twoFactorNudge.requiredMessage: Add an authenticator app as a second factor {{deadline}}. After that, this dashboard stays locked until you finish enrolling.
twoFactorNudge.blockedTitle: Admin access is locked until you set up two-factor authentication
twoFactorNudge.blockedMessage: Your enrollment window has closed, so admin actions are being refused. Set up an authenticator app now to get this dashboard back.
twoFactorNudge.configurable: An admin who has already enrolled can change this policy under Settings in the admin dashboard.

users.title: Users
users.description: Invite new members, change roles, archive, or permanently delete accounts.
users.roleUpdateFailed: Couldn't update that role. Try again.
users.archiveFailed: Couldn't archive that user. Try again.
users.restoreFailed: Couldn't restore that user. Try again.
users.deleteFailed: Couldn't delete that user. Try again.
users.inviteDescription: Creates the account and emails the new user a one-time link to choose their password. If email isn't configured, you get the link to share with them instead. Nobody, including you, is shown a password.
users.revealEmailedDescription: {{email}} has been emailed a link to choose their password. The link works once and expires {{expires}}. After that, they can use “Forgot password?” on the sign-in page.
users.revealNotEmailedDescription: The account for {{email}} was created, but no email was sent. Send them this link through another channel so they can choose their password.
users.setPasswordLinkHint: The link works once and expires {{expires}}. It is only shown here. If it expires unused, send them a new one with “Send password link…” in the user's actions.
users.passwordLinkConfirmDescription: {{email}} gets a one-time link to choose a new password, and any earlier link stops working. Their current password keeps working until the link is used. With email configured the link goes only to their address; otherwise it is shown to you once to pass on privately. Either way, this is recorded in the server log.
users.passwordLinkFailed: Couldn't create a password link. Try again.
users.passwordLinkEmailedDescription: {{email}} has been emailed a link to choose a new password. The link works once and expires {{expires}}.
users.passwordLinkNotEmailedDescription: No email was sent. Send {{email}} this link through a private channel so they can choose a new password. Don't use it yourself: it sets their password.
users.passwordLinkHint: The link works once and expires {{expires}}. It is only shown here. If it expires unused, send a new one.
users.deleteDescription: This permanently deletes the account, its sessions, packages, conversations, SSH keys, tokens and OAuth connections. This cannot be undone. Archive the account to preserve its data.
users.typeEmailToConfirm: Type the user's email to confirm

storage.title: Storage
storage.description: Every clone and checkout on disk. Admins see sizes and owners, never packages, notes or conversations.

usage.title: Disk used
usage.description: Clones and checkouts against COCKPIT_CONTEXT_MAX_STORAGE_GB. Over the cap, pruning removes the least recently used checkouts until usage is under 90 %.

prune.queued: Prune queued. It re-measures every clone and checkout, then frees space if storage is over the cap.
prune.failed: Couldn’t queue the prune. Try again.

repositories.title: Repositories
repositories.description: Expand a repository to see its checkouts. Deleting frees space; the next question clones or checks out again.
repositories.emptyBody: The first question about a package clones its repository here.

checkouts.caption: Checkouts of {{url}}
checkouts.truncated: Showing the {{shown}} most recently used of {{count}} checkouts.

delete.repositoryDescription_one: This deletes the clone and its {{count}} checkout. Packages that use it keep working: the next question clones it again.
delete.repositoryDescription_other: This deletes the clone and its {{count}} checkouts. Packages that use it keep working: the next question clones it again.
delete.checkoutDescription: This frees its disk space. The next question about this version checks it out again.
delete.leasedWarning: A running question is reading this. Deleting it now stops that question.
delete.typeUrl: Type the repository URL to confirm:
delete.typeCommit: Type the short commit to confirm:

storage.snapshotsOverCap: Storage exceeds the cap. Automatic pruning preserves snapshot clones; remove snapshots manually or raise the cap if pruning cannot free enough space.
storage.snapshotDeleteWarning: This snapshot cannot be restored without the owner’s SSH key.

jobs.title: Jobs
jobs.description: Background work: clones, prunes, summaries, cleanups. Failed jobs can be retried.
jobs.emptyBody: Jobs appear here as the server schedules them.
jobs.retryFailed: Couldn’t retry that job. Try again.
